The core insight is that Group II rats utilize an inferential closure mechanism where B is not treated as an independent node but as the logical reverse of A. This allows them to perform a form of deductive reasoning about path efficiency. The mathematical structure resembles a directed graph with a symmetric edge set, where A → B and B → A are functionally equivalent under certain conditions. The inference process involves computing a posterior probability over path costs, effectively modeling a Bayesian update on spatial knowledge. The failure mode arises when the symmetry is broken or when the rat lacks sufficient prior exposure to establish the dual relationship. This leads to increased exploration of B, indicating a lack of closure. The epistemic trace reveals that the rats operate within a closed-loop system of perception-action, where each new segment of the maze contributes to a cumulative model of the environment’s topology.
